name: Soft Natural Lingerie
summary: The soft underwear of the youth years: a sheer, unwired bra with no pad and no seam, stretch bodysuits and tights. They are cut to follow the natural body and to show no line under the dress.

philosophy.core_thesis: Underwear should follow the body and not shape it: a soft cup, a thin cloth and a skin tone that shows no line.
design_principles: Cut the cup from one piece of sheer stretch cloth, with no pad and no wire.
Match the cloth to the skin tone, so that the garment shows no line under thin dress.
Knit the body in nylon tricot or elastane, so that it stretches 50 to 100 per cent and recovers.
Keep the seams to a minimum: one at the side, one at the centre, and no bone.
Make the garment light: 40 to 120 g/m² for the cup and the band.
Fasten with a simple hook at the back or no fastening at all.
Name the garment for what it is: a soft bra, a bodysuit, a pair of tights.
anti_patterns: A thick pad that gives a fixed shape
A girdle that holds the hip flat

silhouette.shape: The natural body line: a soft bust, an open waist and a light, smooth hip.
silhouette.line: A round, soft line with no point and no ridge; the garment follows the body.
silhouette.fit: Light and close; the stretch cloth lies on the skin and moves with it.
silhouette.proportion: Cup depth follows the bust; band 4 to 8 cm; bodysuit rise to the waist; leg to the upper thigh.
rules: Cut the cup from one soft piece with no pad.
Use a thin elastic band at the lower edge of the cup.
Keep the neck and the back low, to suit a dress with a plunge or a bare back.
Cut the bodysuit in one piece with a snap at the crotch.
Choose a skin tone, or a pale colour, so that the line is hard to see.

fabrics.rule: Use thin, stretch knits of nylon and elastane, with a little lace, and keep out all bone and pad.

methods: tricot knit with stretch in two ways
narrow elastic band at the lower edge
snap closure at the crotch of the bodysuit
construction.closures: A single hook at the back, a snap at the crotch of the bodysuit, or no closure on a pull-on garment.
construction.details: A narrow lace at the neck, a thin clear strap, a small label, and a smooth band with no bone.

surface.pattern: Plain skin tones and pastels; a small print or a stripe on the tights and the bodysuit.
surface.gloss: Matte tricot at 4–10 GU; sheer nylon at 15–30 GU.
surface.wear: The elastane loses its stretch after many washes, and the cloth pills at the seam.

palette.strategy: Skin tones, white and pale pastels for underwear; stronger colour only on tights and bodysuits that show.

processes: nylon tricot knitted on a warp machine
narrow elastic set by a machine
dye of the cloth to a range of skin tones
making.scale: Made in a factory in many sizes. The first versions came from a fashion designer and a bra maker, and a mass market followed within a few years.
making.signs: A single-piece cup with no seam at the point, no wire and no pad, a thin band, and a plain label.

pieces.form: Soft-cup bra of sheer nylon tricot, with no wire, no pad and no point seam
One-piece stretch bodysuit with a snap at the crotch
Sheer tights knitted in one piece
Slip of sheer tricot with a narrow lace at the hem

positive: flat packshot on a plain ground

canonical_works.work: No-side bra with a narrow stretch band

emotion.target_response: A sense of ease and honesty: a natural body line, light cloth and no hidden structure.

use_cases: a museum label or object study
avoid_when: the brief wants a pointed bullet bra
the brief is a boned corset

modifiers.how: Add the circle-stitched cup, the boning and the elastic panel of the 1950s foundation.
Keep the soft cup and the skin tone, and pair it with a short, straight dress and tights.

ornament_level.note: The style is plain; a little lace or print is the limit.
